long_biography.plain_text:
Sheikh Ahmed's enduring public identity spans private investment and sport. He is group chairman of A.R.M. Holding, a private investment and real-estate company with property platforms and investments across several sectors. Public material identifies the group with him, but does not disclose his personal stake or support converting its portfolio into a personal net-worth estimate.

His association with Al Wasl began when he played for its predecessor and later became club president. He established Jebel Ali Racecourse, whose track and grandstand opened in 1990, and built a racehorse operation known for yellow silks. His first major winner, Wassl, won the 1982 Irish 2,000 Guineas; Mtoto became another standout. These ownership and leadership interests are documented separately from his royal-family status and public-security role.

uncertainties.detail: The exact person is accepted at very high confidence through the combined A.R.M., Al Wasl and Jebel Ali anchors. Similar names including Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, the Emirates Group chairman, and Sheikh Ahmed bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Dubai's second deputy ruler, were explicitly rejected.

The source record says 7 May 1950 and birth country United Arab Emirates. The dedicated Wikipedia entry instead says 12 July 1950 and Bur Dubai, while other family summaries vary even on the year. No authoritative independent source located confirms the exact day, month or city, so the stored date is not corrected and the alternatives remain review candidates below threshold.

Official and corporate material identifies A.R.M. Holding as Sheikh Ahmed's private investment and real-estate group and identifies him as group chairman; Dun & Bradstreet lists him as Dubai Real Estate Centre's proprietor. Public sources do not disclose precise ownership percentages, shareholder registers or the proportion of his personal wealth represented by each company.

A.R.M. Holding's investments and the more than 3,200 units managed by Dubai Real Estate Centre are company-level or managed-portfolio facts. They are not treated as a list of Sheikh Ahmed's personally titled properties or converted into a personal net-worth estimate.

Current private real-estate interests are documented above threshold, but their original funding and transfer mechanism are not. Real estate remains a below-threshold wealth-creation candidate, and dynastic or royal remains a below-threshold origin candidate; neither royal lineage nor public office is substituted for evidence of a personal fortune.

The deputy-chairman role in Dubai Police and Public Security is used only as an identity cross-check and is not classified as a wealth source. Al Wasl leadership and Jebel Ali racing are described as durable activities; the racecourse and horses are not used to infer the scale of his wider wealth.

No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was verified. The existing Wikipedia URL is retained, and A.R.M. Holding's canonical site is proposed only as a company website. No dedicated Forbes profile was found.
Politics beyond minimal identity context, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, irrelevant private-family detail, personal-net-worth estimates and vessel research are excluded.
